source.extractionNote: One of four independent components on the Chip page, each with its own board and its own metadata frame; this spec covers Filter Chip only. All 16 variants extracted to full depth and diffed against the default. The check mark exists only in active=true variants (an added node, not a hidden one). No on-page private subcomponents.

summary: Lets someone narrow a set of content by switching criteria on and off, such as categories in a list of results. Use them in groups where more than one can be on at once. Reach for an assist chip when the control triggers an action rather than a filter.

label.intent: The criterion the chip switches. Name the filter, not the result. A chip reading Show only items in stock is doing a sentence's work.

intent.false: The filter is off and the chip shows its label alone.
intent.true: The filter is on. This is the real switch for a filter chip, and the only value that both adds the check mark and flips to the inverse palette. Built only alongside State=default and State=focus, so an active chip has no hover or dragged appearance.

intent.default: The resting chip, and where placed instances should stay.
intent.focus: Keyboard focus, and the only state carrying a visible outline.
intent.selected: A second way to show a chosen chip, separate from active. It darkens the background without adding the check mark, so a row mixing selected and active will not read consistently. Prefer active until that overlap is resolved.
intent.dragged: The chip while it is being moved, for filter rows that can be reordered. It reuses the pressed background rather than carrying a token of its own.

state.note: hover and focus are interaction states in code; dragged comes from a reorder interaction; selected overlaps active (see issues).

intent.true: The criterion cannot be switched right now. Say why nearby, because the chip itself gives no other clue.
Match the contour of the controls around the filter row rather than deciding per chip.
intent.false: The square-cornered pairing, for surfaces built from sharp controls.

anatomy.role: The component frame. A horizontal auto-layout hugging its content at a fixed height.
The leading icon, present only when active is true. It is what makes the on state readable without colour.
anatomy.color: currentColor (follows the label colour; not a token on the chip)

anatomy.role: The criterion itself, and the only content the chip takes.
anatomy.note: The text box is trimmed to cap height (measured 8Px tall against a 14Px line). In CSS this is text-box-trim / leading-trim; without it the label is taller and the fixed height still holds.

variants._note: 16 of 40 combinations are built. active=true exists only with state=default and state=focus; disabled=true only with state=default and active=false. Rounded changes only the four corner radii. Height is a fixed 32Px everywhere (unbound).

tokens._note: All 21 token names resolve in tokens/base. The glyph check-mark is in packages/icons/codepoints.json (setId 2046:6876), not retired, not rejected.

states.whatChanges: interactive/neutral/background/default behind a 1px inside border in interactive/neutral/border/default.
Background moves to interactive/neutral/background/hover. Nothing else changes.
Background moves to interactive/neutral/background/focused and the border becomes 2px focus/outline drawn outside the chip.
Background moves to interactive/neutral/background/selected. Border and label are unchanged and no check mark appears.
Background moves to interactive/neutral/background/pressed, the same token a pressed state would use.
Background becomes interactive/neutral/background/disabled, the label drops to the disabled foreground, and the border is removed.

behavior.description: Figma stores no timing and no transition is authored. Turning a filter on is a flat swap of fill, text colour and the presence of the check mark.
active is what switches the filter. It replaces the neutral palette with interactive/inverse and inserts a leading check mark, which also changes the chip's vertical padding and its gap.
Sixteen of the forty possible combinations are built. active=true exists only with State=default and State=focus, so hovering or dragging an active chip is not drawn.

content.description: Plain text set per instance, defaulting to Label. The only text the chip takes.

content.type: nested Icon, present when active is true
content.description: An Icon at Size=small swapped to Check Mark, inserted before the label. It is not a slot and carries no property of its own on the chip.
There is no trailing slot. A filter chip cannot carry a count or a remove control without detaching.

do: Use active to turn a filter on. It is the only value that both recolours the chip and shows the check mark.
Keep filter chips in a group where more than one can be on. A single chip that toggles is usually a switch or a checkbox.
dont: Don't mix State=selected with active in one row. They are two different ways to look chosen and they do not match.
Don't rely on the colour flip alone for the on state. The check mark is what carries it.

accessibility: An active chip carries a check mark as well as the inverse palette, which is what keeps the on state readable without colour. Do not remove it.
State=selected shows a chosen chip through colour alone with no check mark, so it fails that test. Prefer active.
Focus is the only state with a visible outline and it is drawn outside the chip, so check it is not clipped by a scrolling filter row.
Each chip is an on and off control. Expose a pressed or checked state, not just a label.
The label uses indicator/medium at 12px over a 14px line. Check it against the inverse palette as well as the neutral one.

layoutTheming.description: 32 tall across all sixteen variants. Width hugs the label, plus the check mark when active.
space/md left and right throughout. Vertically space/sm when active is false and space/xs when it is true, because the 16px check is taller than the label.
space/xs when active is false, space/sm when true.
radius/pill when true and radius/none when false.
interactive/neutral/background at default, hover, focused, selected and disabled, with pressed reused for dragged. active=true overrides all of it with interactive/inverse/background/selected.
1px inside interactive/neutral/border/default at rest. Focus swaps to 2px focus/outline drawn outside. active=true uses interactive/inverse/border/pressed. Disabled carries none.

indicator/medium, IBM Plex Sans Medium 12 over a 14px line, in interactive/neutral/foreground/default, dropping to the disabled token and flipping to interactive/inverse/foreground/default when active.

visualReference.policy: No images are stored; every node deep-links into Figma so a shot can be pulled on demand and is never stale.

issues.detail: Metadata says space/xs for the active vertical padding and the inactive gap. The bindings are space/xxs, the old 4px space/xs after the rename.

Two ways to look chosen: State=selected (fill only, no check) and active=true (inverse palette plus check). The metadata itself says to prefer active. Recommend modelling only active (as a pressed/checked toggle) in code and leaving selected out until design resolves the overlap.

active=true has no hover, dragged or disabled variant; disabled has no hover/focus. Code needs a decision for hovering an active chip (e.g. keep the active fill) and for an active chip that is disabled.

Root height is a fixed 32px with no token, in all 16 variants. Input Chip binds its height to control/target-min; this one is raw. Hug the content in code (padding plus the 16px icon gives the same height when active) or add a control token.

The 1px inside border is included in layout and the 2px outside focus border is not, so focused and disabled chips are 2px narrower (measured 56 → 54) and content shifts 1px horizontally. Height is fixed, so only width moves. In code keep borders out of layout.

The label uses cap-height leading trim (text box measured 8px tall against a 14px line). That is why padding space/sm plus the label lands inside 32px. Without trim, content is taller; the fixed height still holds.
Stroke-weight bindings are absent in the two disabled variants only because the stroke is removed there (and strokeAlign is left at CENTER). Expected.
No trailing slot (no count, no remove) and no leading slot other than the fixed check mark.
No duplicate among existing specs. Closest neighbours are Checkbox and Switch for a single on/off; the metadata routes single toggles there.
